transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. That's considered light exercise, which is fine to do.

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise, and also avoid swimming for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions for me?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that! When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure whether it's okay to use in your specific case, I'd recommend checking with your GP or care team to be certain.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the information! I've been feeling very sensitive to bright light lately. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity — especially if your eye is also red and painful — that's not normal, and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Does that help? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that helps a lot! Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry beyond that first week, or if it's getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery? That will help me give you a better idea of what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week and a half ago, so it's good to know my vision should be improving soon. Thank you so much for all the information. I don't have any more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! Just to confirm — have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've been very helpful! Thank you for addressing all my questions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!
